key_findings: LLMs achieved perfect sensitivity (1.000) on the balanced development dataset while maintaining precision up to 0.927, outperforming human reviewers (sensitivity 0.775, precision 0.911).

However, while low precision values (4–20%) mean that some irrelevant records were still passed to human reviewers, these performance metrics suggest that the LLM could reduce the volume of records requiring manual review by nearly 80%.

key_findings: Prompt development required 1045 records and achieved 100% sensitivity for studies ultimately included after full-text screening.
Sensitivity for title/abstract decisions varied from 58% to 100% across updates, but no eligible studies were missed.
Precision ranged from 4% to 20%, indicating many irrelevant records were still passed to human reviewers.
Simulated workload reductions of 65–85% were observed, potentially reducing manual screening time by up to 80%.
The LLM demonstrated high consistency in inclusion/exclusion decisions across repeated runs.
